next_changelog: [Never Segment]: added three positionally-specific conditions matching the critic's measured over-segmentation/wrong-boundary cases: (1) never split immediately before a sentence-final trailing fragment that lacks a full predicate (a bare object/noun phrase with no following verb), (2) never carve out a standalone one-word discourse-filler segment — attach it to the clause that follows, (3) when a clause is followed by a reporting/quotative connective such as -했더니/-하니까/-라고 하길래 that introduces the next clause, the boundary belongs BEFORE that connective, not after it, so the connective stays with the clause it introduces rather than being stranded with the clause before it.

[Decision Procedure]: extended step 2's checklist with three matching tests — (f) does B consist only of a trailing verb-less fragment (bare noun/object with no predicate)? (g) is A a single short discourse filler being isolated as its own segment? (h) does the candidate boundary fall right after a reporting/quotative connective that actually introduces B, meaning the tag should instead be placed immediately before that connective? — so the reject/move logic operationalizes the newly added [Never Segment] conditions without banning any connective form outright.

next_changelog: [Core Principles]: added three precise WHERE-conditions targeting the critic's measured wrong-boundary/over-segmentation cases — never strand a verb-less trailing fragment, never isolate a single filler word as its own segment, and place the boundary BEFORE a reporting/quotative connective (e.g. -했더니) rather than after it — folded into the existing 'when in doubt, split' bullet so these read as conditions on WHERE a safe cut sits, not blanket bans on any connective form. This avoids repeating the rejected v3 change, which added the same ideas to [Never Segment]+[Decision Procedure] and over-restricted latency; here they are scoped narrowly (verb-less trailing fragment, single-word filler, reporting connective) with no effect on ordinary clause splits.

[When to Segment]: added five concrete permissive cues directly answering the critic's under-segmentation evidence (missed_gain cases that already passed the quality floor): causal -어서/아서 when both sides are independently complete, sequential 나중에/-고 나서 markers, opinion-introducing phrases like 내 생각에는, embedded '?' followed by an independent resumption clause, and a topic-shifting 이제 immediately before a self-contained final clause. These are stated as general surface conditions, not sentence-specific rules, and target boundaries INSIDE previously-unsplit long sentences rather than adding more short pieces elsewhere.
